title: Jesus! and Shall It Ever Be
description: Jesus! and Shall It Ever Be in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Joseph Grigg wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 504 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Not Ashamed of Christ”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-sus! and shall it ev-er be! A mor-tal man a-shamed of thee; A-shamed of thee, whom an-gels praise, Whose glo-ries shine through end-less days!

lines: Jesus! and shall it ever be!
A mortal man ashamed of thee;
Ashamed of thee, whom angels praise,
Whose glories shine through endless days!
Ashamed of Jesus! just as soon
Let midnight be ashamed of noon;
'Tis midnight with my soul, till he,
Bright morning star, bid darkness flee.
Ashamed of Jesus! yes I may,
When I've no guilt to wash away,
No tear to wipe — no good to crave,
No fears to quell — no soul to save.
Till then — nor is my boasting vain —
Till then, I boast a Saviour slain;
And oh! may this my glory be,
That Christ is not ashamed of me.

licence: Public domain: Joseph Grigg died in 1768.
credits: Words by Joseph Grigg (1720–1768), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
